what_it_does: Modern graphics memory (GDDR7) needs to receive data at very high speeds—42 gigabits per second—without errors even when the electrical signals blur together. This paper describes a receiver that uses a hybrid decision-feedback equalization technique to clean up distorted incoming signals. The receiver runs at 42 gigabits per second, transmitting 3 levels per symbol (called PAM3). It combines direct-feedback and loop-unrolled approaches to balance the tradeoff between speed (feedback must happen within nanoseconds) and chip area, enabling fast-enough feedback timing while keeping power and space overhead low.
